result.topic_en: Transformations of the hypergeometric differential equation for F(α,β,γ,x): the Wronskian-type relation, the substitution x = t/(t−1) giving the Pfaff/Euler transformation to argument −x/(1−x), and the expression of F(α,β,γ,1/x) in terms of functions of argument x.
result.transcription:
46

zweitens dass $-\left(\frac{\gamma-(\alpha+\beta+1)x}{x-xx}\right)dx = \partial\log(QdP-PdQ)$
also
$\frac{QdP-PdQ}{dx} = \frac{A}{x^\gamma(1-x)^{\alpha+\beta+1-\gamma}}$

Noch eine wichtige Verwandlung vollführt man auf folgende Art:
Man setze $x=\frac{t}{t-1}$, also $\frac{dx}{dt}=-\frac{1}{(t-1)^2}$, $\frac{d^2x}{dt^2}=\frac{2}{(t-1)^3}$
Hiedurch verwandelt sich die Gleichung für $F(\alpha,\beta,\gamma,x)=P$ in

$\frac{\alpha\beta}{t-1}P-(\gamma+(\alpha+\beta+1-\gamma)t)\frac{dP}{dt}-(t-tt)\frac{d^2P}{dt^2}=0$
Macht man also $P=(t-1)^\mu P'$ so wird

$\frac{\alpha\beta-\gamma\mu+\mu t(\gamma-\alpha-\beta+\mu)}{t-1}P'-(\gamma+(\alpha+\beta-1-\gamma-2\mu)t)\frac{dP'}{dt}-(t-tt)\frac{d^2P'}{dt^2}=0$

Um den Bruch wegzuschaffen, setzt man $\alpha\beta-\alpha\mu-\beta\mu+\mu\mu=0$, also entweder
$\mu=\alpha$ oder $\mu=\beta$. Im ersten Fall wird
$(-\alpha\beta+\alpha\gamma)P'-(\gamma-(\gamma+1+\alpha-\beta)t)\frac{dP'}{dt}-(t-tt)\frac{d^2P'}{dt^2}=0$
woraus
$P'=\mathfrak{A}'F(\alpha,\gamma-\beta,\gamma,t)+\mathfrak{B}'(\alpha,\gamma-\beta,\alpha+1-\beta,1-t)$
Hieraus folgert man leicht
$F(\alpha,\beta,\gamma,x)=(1-x)^{-\alpha}F(\alpha,\gamma-\beta,\gamma,-\frac{x}{1-x})$
$=(1-x)^{-\beta}F(\beta,\gamma-\alpha,\gamma,-\frac{x}{1-x})$
Mit Hülfe dieser Verwandlung kann man die Werthe unsrer Functionen für negative x auf die Werthe für positive reduciren.

$F(\alpha,\beta,\gamma,\frac{1}{x})=Ax^\alpha F(\alpha,\alpha+1-\gamma,\alpha+1-\beta,x)+Bx^\beta F(\beta,\beta+1-\gamma,\beta+1-\alpha,x)$
$A=(\cos\alpha\pi+i\sin\alpha\pi)\frac{\Pi(\gamma-1).\Pi(\beta-1-\alpha)}{\Pi(\beta-1)\Pi(\gamma-1-\alpha)}$
$B=(\cos\beta\pi+i\sin\beta\pi)\frac{\Pi(\gamma-1).\Pi(\alpha-1-\beta)}{\Pi(\alpha-1)\Pi(\gamma-1-\beta)}$

methods.what: Wronskian of two solutions of the hypergeometric equation (Abel–Liouville formula)
Change of variable x = t/(t−1) in the hypergeometric equation
Substitution P=(t−1)^μ P' with μ chosen to remove the fraction (μ=α or μ=β)

methods.what: General solution of the reduced equation as combination of hypergeometric functions in t and 1−t
Pfaff transformation of the hypergeometric function
Connection formula for F at argument 1/x in terms of functions at x, with Gamma (Π) function coefficients

items.english: From this one easily concludes F(α,β,γ,x) = (1−x)^{−α} F(α,γ−β,γ,−x/(1−x)).

items.quote: Mit Hülfe dieser Verwandlung kann man die Werthe unsrer Functionen für negative x auf die Werthe für positive reduciren.
items.english: With the help of this transformation one can reduce the values of our functions for negative x to the values for positive x.
F(α,β,γ,1/x) equals A x^α F(α,α+1−γ,α+1−β,x) + B x^β F(β,β+1−γ,β+1−α,x), with A and B as given.
